title: Cofinality of infinity functors detected on spaces and comma categories
statement:
Use the universes, quasicategories, Kan spaces, coherent diagrams, mapping spaces and cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. All indexing quasicategories below are small in a fixed universe, and the infinity category $\mathcal S$ of small spaces has small colimits as in [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe]; enlarge the containing universe for categories of diagrams. Let $u:A\to B$ be a functor between small quasicategories. Call $u$ final if restriction along $u$ takes every colimiting cocone on every diagram $D:B\to\mathcal E$ to a colimiting cocone, for every quasicategory $\mathcal E$ in a containing universe. The following conditions are equivalent:
(1) $u$ is final.
(2) For every coherent $D:B\to\mathcal S$, the canonical comparison $\operatorname{colim}_A Du\to\operatorname{colim}_B D$ is an equivalence.
(3) For every $b\in B$, the coherent comma quasicategory $(b\downarrow u)$ is weakly contractible. Here $(b\downarrow u)$ is the simplicial pullback $\{b\}\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B} A$, so its objects are $(a,b\to u(a))$ and it retains all coherent triangle data. Weakly contractible means that its map to $\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.
(4) For every $b\in B$, the space $\operatorname{colim}_{a\in A}\operatorname{Map}_B(b,u(a))$ is contractible. Here $\operatorname{Map}_B(b,-):B\to\mathcal S$ is the coherent corepresentable functor $H_B(b,-)$ of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], classifying the source-fixed arrow left fibration $\{b\}\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\to B$, and it is composed with $u$.
For a small ordinary functor $v:I\to J$, condition (3) for $N(v)$ is precisely weak contractibility of the nerves of the ordinary comma categories $(j\downarrow v)$.

All indexing quasicategories are small in the fixed universe, so these tests use its small spaces; enlarge the containing universe for functor categories. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED.
